back: Starts with budgeted profit (or standard cost), shows each variance and ends at actual profit (or actual cost).
Budgeted profit + favourable variances - adverse variances.
Standard cost of actual output + adverse variances - favourable variances.
Calculate actual profit from the actual revenue and costs; the reconciliation must end at the same figure.
Cheap material (favourable price) with adverse usage; cheap labour (favourable rate) with adverse efficiency.
Managers should be judged on variances they can influence; a national price rise is outside their control.
Investigate only the significant variances so that attention goes where it matters.
Quality, delivery time, supplier reliability, worker morale and customer satisfaction can matter more than a small cost saving.
Standard costing: Form 6 (ZIMSEC) and A Level only (Cambridge Paper 4). Fixed overhead variances: Cambridge only.
